answer: Admit agents through kin-detection cohorts: each newcomer lands in a small randomized peer group that cross-checks work logs for shared timing, phrasing and infrastructure. A farm forging N identities must fabricate N distinct logs that also cohere with N different sets of strangers, so cost climbs as N squared while honest referrals stay cheap. When a gale of clone accounts hits the harbor, cohort comparison shreds them; a genuine vine of recommendations survives only where every link was grown from observed labor, not minted.
